articles.title: Zach Cregger Says He Feels Like He's 'Running for Office' Trying to Get Skeptical Resident Evil Fans 'Not to Call Me a LARPer'
articles.summary: Resident Evil director Zach Cregger has said he feels like he’s been on an “apology tour” while navigating skepticism from some fans about his movie adaptation of Capcom’s horror franchise.
body: Cregger, director of hugely popular horror movies Barbarian and Weapons, has faced scrutiny from Resident Evil fans ever since it was confirmed that his adaptation wouldn’t feature any characters from the video games, or tell any of the stories already told in the video games. Instead, Cregger has charted his own path, telling a horror story set in the world of Resident Evil that references some of the video games' tropes.
In an interview with The Playlist, Cregger outlined how it has felt to promote Resident Evil amid this backlash.
“I feel like I’ve been on somewhat of an apology tour,” he said. “I feel like I’m running for office, trying to get these people not to call me a LARPer.”

With Resident Evil now just a week away, Cregger is philosophical about fan attitude to the film. “Now, I’m just like, ‘You know what? See the movie.’” he told The Playlist. “If you still feel the same way after you’ve seen it, then whatever you think is fair. You’re going to decide if I’m an actual Resident Evil fan or a fake. What can I say? I think the movie is going to speak for itself.”
points: Resident Evil director Zach Cregger has said he feels like he’s been on an “apology tour” while navigating skepticism from some fans about his movie adaptation of Capcom’s horror franchise.

articles.title: Exodus Ending and Character Fates Change Based on Your Choices
articles.summary: Any time you look at or talk about Exodus, the upcoming space opera RPG from Archetype Entertainment, the Mass Effect comparisons start flying at light speed. I mean, Exodus narrative director Drew Karpyshyn played a major role as a writer and lead at BioWare to shape the stories of its biggest…
body: The parallels don't end with the Paladin/Immortal morality system or the romance and relationship dynamics that are going to drive the story, either. He hinted at how the decisions you make can impact Exodus' ending. Of course, that's not exclusive to BioWare games by any stretch, but when the Mass Effect 2's suicide mission is regarded as a series pinnacle, no one would blame to draw a quick comparison.

When I asked about the relationship systems in Exodus, Karpyshyn emphasized wanting to make them feel real and said it's about, "[M]aking their relationship with you grow, allowing it to evolve from the choices you've made, and realizing that the choices you make are going to bring some companions closer to you, but maybe push some companions farther away."

He took it one step further, and told me, "Without spoiling too much, we definitely want to have it impact how their storylines go." Then he took it another step further and concluded, "Depending on choices you make, by the end of the game, you might not have every companion with you that you started with. That's about all I can say!"
points: Any time you look at or talk about Exodus, the upcoming space opera RPG from Archetype Entertainment, the Mass Effect comparisons start flying at light speed.
The parallels don't end with the Paladin/Immortal morality system or the romance and relationship dynamics that are going to drive the story, either.

articles.title: Official Backrooms 2 Announcement Reportedly Happening Soon, With Kane Parsons Returning
articles.summary: Dread Central reports that a sequel to Backrooms is in the works and that Kane Parsons has been signed as director. According to the horror media outlet, fans can expect an announcement soon.
body: Backrooms was born from a picture of a strange, liminal space that caught the eye of Kane Parsons, who then turned it into a horror web series on YouTube that went viral. This led A24 to pick up the project and turn it into an indie horror film, which was directed by the YouTuber himself. The movie proved just as popular as the web series, as Backrooms grossed nearly $400 million globally — about 40 times its production budget.

In an interview with Variety back in May, director Kane Parsons hinted at a possible sequel: " Backrooms has always been planned to be more of a series that goes outside the confines of this film...I've got a contract, and I got a hold at my end, and that means I am definitely not done with Backrooms." It now seems that the sequel might be moving forward sooner than anyone expected. Dread Central says that "an official announcement is imminent" and that it has confirmation that " Backrooms 2 will be Parsons' next movie."

articles.title: Riot Co-Founder Calls League of Legends MMO the 'Grail' Quest, 5 Years After It Was Announced
articles.summary: League of Legends developer Riot Games is still bashing away on its MMO, which co-founder Mark Merrill recently described as the studio’s “grail quest.” Riot announced its MMO five years ago, in August 2021.
body: “We know what players’ hopes and dreams are,” he said. “It’s just on us as a team, and can we succeed in the execution?”
Merrill said Riot jokingly calls the MMO the “grail” because “f**k it, many a brave knight are gonna die on the grail quest. But f**k it, it’s the grail, so let’s go.”
“That’s the mindset that we really try to cultivate. And that is hard to do at scale,” he continued. “But I think we’re doing a reasonable job. And I think the future’s incredibly bright.”

It’s fair to say Merrill’s comments were met with a healthy dose of skepticism, particularly from fighting game fans. Riot recently announced its League of Legends fighting game, 2XKO, ends active development at the end of this year due to a lack of players. It only released late 2025, so you can understand where this sentiment is coming from.
points: League of Legends developer Riot Games is still bashing away on its MMO, which co-founder Mark Merrill recently described as the studio’s “grail quest.

articles.title: Skytech Gaming Blaze 5 Review
articles.summary: The Skytech Gaming Blaze 5 is packed with strong mid-tier components in a sleek glassy tower, but there are a few issues that’ll impact your quality of life.
body: A custom pre-built gaming PC like the Skytech Gaming Blaze 5 is going to save you a lot of work if you’re not technically savvy or simply don’t have the patience to put together a modern-day puzzle. With its Nvidia GeForce RTX 5070 graphics card and AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D, you’re getting solid mid-tier performance. And it’s all packed away in an easy-to-open glass case with shiny RGB components.

That said, it’s not without issue. Upgrading or replacing components is likely going to take moving a few things out of the way, as it’s a bit crowded on the motherboard. Even if you don’t plan on upgrading, you’ll either be annoyed by the finicky RGB lighting or the fact that the power button and front ports are at the very bottom of the tower, making floor placement very awkward. These may not be dealbreakers for some, but you should know what you’re getting into.
points: The Skytech Gaming Blaze 5 is packed with strong mid-tier components in a sleek glassy tower, but there are a few issues that’ll impact your quality of life.

articles.title: Farming Sims Are Finally Changing After 10 Years of Stagnation
articles.summary: Farm-sims have looked and played pretty much the same for the last 10 years. That's not entirely surprising. When you find a winning formula that keeps your studio's lights on, you follow that formula.
body: In 2016, Stardew Valley reignited interest in a genre that had largely lost its mainstream appeal, after the glorious summer days of Harvest Moon and Story of Seasons faded into distant memories. A trickle of other new farm games started appearing, and even Marvelous, the Story of Seasons studio, revived its biggest hit, Friends of Mineral Town (a remake of the GBA game that was a remake of Harvest Moon 64, the latter of which inspired Stardew Valley ). The trickle became a flood as interest in cozy games skyrocketed during the pandemic, but while they varied in substance, most were largely the same in form.
points: Farm-sims have looked and played pretty much the same for the last 10 years.
When you find a winning formula that keeps your studio's lights on, you follow that formula.

articles.title: Sony Can't Hide Forever
articles.summary: Patch Notes is a weekly newsletter bringing you the best of Polygon, sent on Fridays and published on the site on Sundays. You can subscribe here.
body: It has never been Sony's style to get out in front of things. That's in contrast to Xbox, which loves to push a loquacious executive — whether it's J Allard, or Peter Moore, or Phil Spencer, or Asha Sharma — out on stage to strut its stuff, explain its thinking, or sometimes, air its dirty laundry.

That's the Silicon Valley way, but it's not Sony's way. Give or take a public mascot like Shuhei Yoshida, the company's business executives have mostly been pretty, well, businesslike for the past 20 years, ever since the infamous car crash of E3 2006. They don't project a lot of personality or straight talk. This suits the PlayStation brand, which likes to present itself as cool, inscrutable, and monolithic.

This week, PlayStation broadcast its latest State of Play showcase. I'd describe it as modest, but well balanced. We got big updates for big games, cool indies, a few genuine left-field surprises, a deeper look at a 2027 blockbuster. We got a Lego PlayStation and a Grand Theft Auto 6 controller.
points: It has never been Sony's style to get out in front of things.

articles.title: Saber Interactive CCO says studio won't change its comms strategy after AI writer controversy
articles.summary: Saber Interactive CCO Tim Willits has confirmed the company has not revised its communications strategy despite its CEO telling the press that he "would have been happy to replace [a writer] with AI" after she claimed she was replaced by ChatGPT.
body: CEO Matthew Karch has since apologised to Stella Sacco, the writer at the centre of the Rideshare Stimulator AI controversy, but not before widespread public condemnation. He also shared a statement saying he'd had an "insightful week" but "the digital ecosystem thrives on outrage and surface-level takes".
"Sometimes we 'say what we mean' too much," Willits told PC Gamer, reflecting on the blunt comms from the studio's leadership.
When PC Gamer pressed directly on whether the recent backlash had prompted reflection, he reportedly said "no".

"I've been in the industry for so long, and there's always some dust up. People got mad at Saber because we put World War Z on Epic, and people were like, 'oh, Saber's destroying the industry'," Willits added.

articles.title: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation Devs Say Ending Is Best 'Not Explained To You By Someone Else'
articles.summary: In a Final Fantasy 7 Remake trilogy panel at PAX West, game director Naoki Hamaguchi and battle director Teruki Endo went into detail about Cid, Vincent, and the FITS combat system that's new in Final Fantasy 7 Revelation.
body: During a panel, a presentation slide about the series' conclusion directly stated, "We hope you experience the climax as something that's not explained to you by someone else, but rather, as something that belongs to you."

The Final Fantasy 7 Revelation battle system stands out in the trilogy due to the introduction of Cid and Vincent and the brand-new FITS system. At PAX West, Teruki Endo went over each of these implementations, giving players an idea of the versatility of each character, FITS selection, and how much it will impact gameplay.

Cid wields a magical lance that can impale multiple opponents at once, and he's an aerial ace that hits harder while airborne. This sets him apart from other party members and makes him perfect for long-range, aerial combat. Vincent uses a gun that suits mid-range combat. He is also a close-range combat master due to his Galian Beast transformation, which allows him to perform a series of melee attacks at any time.

articles.title: Do you ever listen to videogame music in your day-to-day life?
articles.summary: You know, I do a lot of prattling about videogame music at this humble website PC Gamer dot com. It's practically woven into the fabric of my very being at this point—hugely formative for me growing up, and now I carry little bits of it everywhere.
body: I have half a dozen VGM playlists dedicated to stuff like the gym, relaxing, and locking in at work. I've formed lifelong memories with friends as we've filled karaoke rooms with the sound of all kinds of Final Fantasy 14 tracks, where our so-called tastes in "regular" music might misalign; we're instead united by our mutual love and attachment to the songs we hear in a game.

In fact, it's so deeply entrenched into my everyday life that I can't imagine any videogame fan not listening to their favourite tunes outside of the game they came from. That is, until I was recently chatting with a friend where they told me just that: even if they really like a song in a videogame, they'll never go out of their way to listen to it detached from its origin.

So that had me wondering—how many of you actually listen to videogame music in your day-to-day life? Does it accompany you while you run errands? Do you have a playlist specifically dedicated to certain tasks or moods filled with songs from all of your favourite games? Or do you just get those random urges to listen to a videogame track that won't leave your head, leaving your YouTube or Spotify history littered with gaming-related earworms?
points: You know, I do a lot of prattling about videogame music at this humble website PC Gamer dot com.
It's practically woven into the fabric of my very being at this point—hugely formative for me growing up, and now I carry little bits of it everywhere.

articles.title: GSC Game World says there's a reason it didn't give Stalker 2 more time in the oven: 'To make something better, you need to receive feedback, and this feedback should be fresh'
articles.summary: Like a lot of survival games, Stalker 2 had a long journey from janky larva to playable, easily recommended butterfly. It's tempting to say that these games ought to just stay under wraps until they're done and relatively bug-free—but at Gamescom 2026, GSC Game World CEO and head of game direction…
body: As for why the studio didn't just wait to release the game until it was in the state it is now, Grygorovych cited both creative and financial reasons. "To make something better, you need to receive feedback, and this feedback should be fresh. From a business perspective, it's also impossible, because it's very expensive to do two years of additional work … in most cases, it's unrealistic."

GSC Game World has more legitimate reasons than most to release an unfinished game. The Ukrainian studio was working on Stalker 2 when development was interrupted by Russia's invasion, forcing the team to move out of Kyiv, and its progress was later hamstrung by a devastating office fire and numerous leaks. And notably, the game's buggy release did arrive after delays —but regardless of all the unique trouble GSC Game World encountered, Grygorovych pointed to woeful market conditions across the board as another consideration.

articles.title: Dutch artist responds to the White House's Build the Wall game with Build that Bridge
articles.summary: A Dutch artist has released Build that Bridge, a free browser game built as a direct response to Build the Wall, the Tetris-style minigame the White House launched on Arcade.Gov last week.
body: The Trump administration's site includes games inspired by old favourites. For example, Rio Run is a Snake-like game that wants you to collect a chain of prisoners in orange jumpsuits, tallying a "deported" count at the end of each run, and Build the Wall: Zombie Border Siege, a Tetris riff where players stack bricks against incoming "aliens" at the "Southern Border".

Whereas the White House version has players stack blocks into a wall, artist and social designer Wouter Sieuwerts's version, Build that Bridge, uses the same mechanics in reverse: clearing lines grows a bridge from both riverbanks toward the middle.
"Just as the colonisation of America was turned into child's play, the White House now makes a game out of excluding migrants," Sieuwerts said.

"But play is precisely how you discover the world and get to know new people and customs. So for everyone who would rather build bridges than walls, I made Build that Bridge. Play along and make yourself heard."

articles.title: The Halloween game has a sex minigame in it, except no it doesn't, because it was apparently removed
articles.summary: If you've seen any slasher flick, you know the drill: every youth is horny, and the horny must die. Despite Halloween not being quite as trope-riddled as some of its stabbiest contemporaries, its recent asymmetrical PvP adaptation did include a minigame where two players could slip into a closet…
body: In fact, it seems to have been silently hotfixed out. The most recent patch notes make no mention of the sex minigame, but the comments sure do. On the Steam thread, one user commented "ADD BACK THE CLOSET MINIGAME" five times in a row. Others have noted that Lynda, a flirty playable civilian who previously got extra benefits from the sex minigame, has had that trait removed, which I can confirm with a quick launch of the game.

Players on social media are not pleased, as you might imagine. "Lame as hell," wrote Choice-Scholar-2297 on Reddit. A thread on the game's subreddit titled "Please add back sex mini game" is quickly gaining traction; freetheree's original post reads, "Why did they remove it!??!?!?!? Me and my homeboy just wanna have sex in a closet? And we can’t???? Tf??????"

Lots of the sorts of jokes you might expect are being thrown around, and of course, it is hilarious that if this change sticks the game will have had closet sex as an exclusive time-limited pre-order bonus. Unfortunately, there might be a good reason for its removal.

articles.title: Double Fine's first game since leaving Xbox is a comedy bus-driving sim called Thank You Bus Driver
articles.summary: Double Fine's first game since leaving Xbox, Thank You Bus Driver, is a comedy sim about a reckless bus driver just trying to be appreciated.
body: Double Fine's first game in its new post-Xbox era is Thank You Bus Driver.

Described as a comedy simulation game, the game - listed only as "coming soon" on Steam - sees you take on the role of a "reckless" bus driver in which you're encouraged to "drive fast, slap faster, and toss any rulebreakers out of your bus to reach true victory: being appreciated".
"Take on the role of a town’s rules-driven (and reckless) bus driver in Thank You Bus Driver!" the Steam description teases.

"Getting to your next stop is all that matters. That might mean pulling up your map mid-turn or it might mean a shortcut through the corn field. Avoiding pedestrians, incoming traffic, or the fence directly in front of you is optional."

articles.title: I never thought a fishing sim could be this fun, but How to Fish proves me wrong with its ridiculous physics, killer spider crabs, and classic co-op chaos
articles.summary: I stand knee deep in a pool of blood. My coworkers, comrades, and friends reduced to food for soulless seagulls. Give a man a fish and he may throw it into the mouth of a weary fisherman, teach a man to fish and he shall bring forth the wrath of a spider crab who knows how to stab you with your own…
body: This was my first experience of the new multiplayer fishing sim How to Fish, and now I can see why it's become such a smash-hit among bored and borderline-violent friendship groups.

It has a simple premise: you and up to four friends learn how to fish. The cycle of work involves players buying a basic fishing rod at first, using this to fish for, well, fish and crustaceans, and then beating them to death with your bare knuckles, brass knuckles, or a sick-ass knife. Then you can either eat your catch to replenish your health or hunger or feed it to the lonely fisherman who sits on the dock and gives you coins for your hard work. With the coins gained you can buy more tools to help you fish, like the knife, or supplies which you can use as bait, such as half a hotdog or an empty beer can.
When I first woke up on the island I was met with a friendly punch in the face.

Some things can be so simple that they become boring, and perhaps How to Fish would fall into this trap, if it were just you and the fisherman on the island. But when you add three other people with nothing to lose and access to friendly-fire things get out of hand in the best way possible.
